msg_value.meaning: native value (msg.value) forwarded by the caller into UnstakeMessenger.unstake()

native_fee.meaning: exact LayerZero native fee fee.nativeFee returned by _quote(hubEid, payload, options, false)

buffered_flow_used.meaning: integrator followed the buffered-fee pattern (used the buffer quote helper and forwarded that buffered value as msg.value)

paynative_reverted.meaning: inherited LayerZero OAppSender._payNative() reverted with NotEnoughNative during the unstake call

message_dispatched.meaning: the LayerZero message was dispatched by the endpoint during the unstake call

claims.scope: core: cross-chain unstake via the buffered-fee flow

preconditions.text: The caller follows the buffered-fee pattern and forwards a msg.value strictly greater than the exact quoted nativeFee as the unstake msg.value.
preconditions.derivation: p_buffered_helper_used supplies buffered_flow_used; p_msg_value_exceeds_exact and p_buffer_greater_than_exact supply the strict msg_value > native_fee; as_quote_is_exact fixes native_fee as the endpoint-required amount.

safety.text: Under the in-scope buffered overpayment premise, payment excess alone must not cause the specified NotEnoughNative fee-mismatch revert.
safety.derivation: Assistant-reviewed control: expresses the intended buffered-payment obligation using the same specific failure observation as V, scoped by P. No claim of full transaction success or exact refund.

effects.text: The buffered-flow unstake reverts: _payNative treats msg.value > fee.nativeFee as a mismatch and reverts with NotEnoughNative before any LayerZero message is dispatched, breaking the call and the exposed buffered pattern for users.
effects.derivation: i_unstake_reverts asserts the NotEnoughNative revert before dispatch; i_buffer_pattern_unusable and i_users_cannot_unstake restate the resulting pattern/user failure. The revert witnesses the violation of excess_tolerated under P.

effect_coverage.reason: Effects conjunction encodes the NotEnoughNative revert together with the absence of LayerZero dispatch.
'Unusable in practice' is the same single-call revert restated for the integration pattern, not an independent resource/measurable.
Captured only for the buffered flow; the report does not establish behavior of any other unstake path.

assumptions: as_quote_is_exact: the fee returned by _quote(hubEid, payload, options, false) is the exact native amount required by the LayerZero endpoint.
The caller forwards the buffered helper's returned value unmodified as msg.value.
msg_value and nativeFee are denominated in the same native-token smallest unit (wei).
The buffered flow with msg.value > nativeFee is the in-scope scenario; the exact-fee flow is treated as out of scope.
unresolved: Whether excess msg.value could be refunded at any point before _payNative() executes is unspecified.
The exact helper set beyond quoteUnstakeWithBuffer()/quoteUnstakeWithReturnValue() is not enumerated.
The exactness identity as_quote_is_exact is an assumption, not an independently sourced endpoint requirement.
Whether the affected code is deployed on a live network or only exercised in tests is not established.
Assistant-derived control, not a new external model extraction; code binding and complete helper/payment/revert semantics remain absent.

limitations: Deferred impact i_ux_path_broken (potential): persistent/population-wide user-facing failure, not a bounded single-call fact; requires review.
Deferred impact i_integrators_must_use_exact: secondary timing/gas-price fragility between quote and execution; not formalizable without timing checkpoints.
Deferred impact i_no_direct_fund_loss: an absence of bad effect, so there is no V to formalize.
Economic impact beyond reverting-call gas consumption (e.g. locked funds) is unspecified; no direct fund loss is claimed.
No adversarial actor is identified; the report describes an integration/design mismatch, not an exploit.
Strict vs non-strict boundary is preserved: unstake() checks msg.value >= fee.nativeFee, while _payNative enforces equality; the violation concerns the latter.
